findings.title: Empty catch swallows fetch/JSON errors in getJson
findings.note: Catch block is completely empty: network failures, non-JSON responses, and auth errors are silently discarded. Caller receives null indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result; no log, no rethrow, nothing to alert anyone the request failed.
findings.proof: The catch at client.ts:11 is genuinely empty — real error-masking as a code pattern. But getJson has zero in-repo callers (confirmed via repo-wide grep and index.ts review), so today no caller receives a masked failure and no one is misled by it in production; the question 'who learns of it' has answer 'no one, because nothing calls this.' The defect is latent, not live, so full severity-5 (production risk) is overstated until the function is wired up.

findings.title: CI wraps entire test suite in automatic retries
findings.note: The whole npm test command is retried up to 3 times at CI level; a failing test can pass on retry, so intermittent test failures are not surfaced as CI failures.

evidence.quote:
- uses: nick-fields/retry@7152eba30c6575329ac0576536151aca5a72780e
        with:
          timeout_minutes: 10
          max_attempts: 3
          command: npm test

findings.proof: ci.yml:15-19 wraps the entire `npm test` invocation in nick-fields/retry with max_attempts: 3, timeout_minutes: 10. This retries the whole suite, not a single flaky assertion, so any intermittently-failing test can pass on attempt 2 or 3 and CI reports green. No test-level retry/quarantine mechanism exists to isolate which test was flaky.

findings.title: Cart total test asserts hardcoded money total with no derivation
findings.note: Asserts against the literal 2000 rather than deriving it from the priced sku/qty inputs used in the test, so a reader must cross-reference the pricing table to know the expectation is correct.
findings.proof: pricing.ts:3 sets PRICES.A1=1000; cart.ts:17 total() sums priceOf(sku)*qty. Test adds A1 qty=2 (1000*2=2000) and asserts toBe(2000) with no reference to the 1000 unit price, so the reader must open pricing.ts to confirm correctness. Not table-driven, no fake timers, and this is the only assertion in the test (not assertion-free).

findings.title: Skipped bulk-pricing test asserts a value the implementation cannot produce
